This Petition, Coming On For Orders, This Day, The
Court Made The Following:
 Order

1. Accused nos.2 to 4 in Crime No.81/2023 registered by Javagal Police Station, Hassan District, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 304B, 34 IPC and Sections 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, are before this Court under Section 438 Cr.PC.

2. Heard the learned Counsel for the parties.
3.

On the complaint of Naveenakumara S/o Billaiah, who is the brother of deceased Abhilasha, FIR in Crime No.81/2023 was registered by Javagal police for the aforesaid offences against Nagesha and three others.
Nagesha is the husband of deceased Abhilasha.
Petitioner no.1 is the father of accused NC: 2023:KHC:45853 no.1.
Petitioner nos.2 & 3 are the maternal uncle and aunt of accused no.1.
Apprehending arrest in the said case, petitioners had filed Crl. Misc. No.1309/2023 before the Court of II Addl. District & Sessions Judge, Hassan, which was dismissed on 09.11.2023.

sentences.text: Learned Counsel for the petitioners submits that from the complaint averments, it is seen that for the last more than 1 1/2 years, the deceased was residing in her parents house.
There is no serious allegation against the petitioners herein who are the close relatives of accused no.1.
They have been falsely implicated in the present case.
They have no criminal antecedents.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the petition.
He submits that investigation in the case is under progress and accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
6. From a reading of the complaint averments, it is seen that the deceased had returned to her parents house when she was about six months pregnant.
As on the date of her death, she had a girl child who was aged about one year two months.
In the complaint, it is averred that after delivery of the said NC: 2023:KHC:45853 child, the deceased was throughout staying in her parents house.
It is averred in the complaint that accused no.1 used to visit the deceased once or twice in a month, but he had not taken her back.
In the complaint, it is averred that accused no.1 was demanding for dowry and was stating that deceased would be taken back only if she brings additional dowry.

However, there is no allegation that after the deceased had returned to her parents house for the purpose of delivery, the petitioners herein had ill-treated her or made any demand for additional dowry.
The allegation against the petitioners is that prior to deceased returning to her parents house, the petitioners used to ill-treat her demanding additional dowry.
Undisputedly, the petitioners have no criminal antecedents.
They are aged persons.
Under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that the petitioners are entitled for the relief of anticipatory bail.

Accordingly, the following order:
7.
The petition is allowed.

The respondent - Police or any other police in the State of Karnataka are directed to release the petitioner in the event of his arrest Crime No.81/2023 registered by Javagal Police Station, Hassan District, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 304B, 34 IPC and NC: 2023:KHC:45853 Sections 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, subject to the following conditions:
1. The Petitioners shall appear before the Investigating Officer within 15 days from the date of receipt of the copy of this order and shall execute a personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
each with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the investigating officer.
2. Petitioners shall regularly appear before the Trial Court without fail unless exempted by the Trial Court for valid reasons.
3. Petitioners shall not tamper with the prosecution witness and he shall co-operate with the police for investigation and appear before them whenever called upon.
4. The petitioners shall not involve in similar offences in future.
